subject: Request for temporary SLA exception due to filter-dependent tool fallbacks (Acme Retail pilot)
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmeretail.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudOps Integrations <cloudops@partner.io>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Observed latency spikes tied to content-filter tool calls (pilot)

Connor —

We saw two production-impacting incidents yesterday during our Acme pilot where checkout personalization API calls slowed to a >2s tail for customers in AP. Initial investigation points to additional tool-call latency when the content-filter path invoked an external moderation model. The application-level SLA we signed with you expects 99.9% request success within 300ms; these spikes are causing meaningful business risk for our conversion tests.

Can Redwood scope a temporary carve-out or mitigation while we sort the filter->tool integration? We're ok with a documented exception window if there are compensating mitigations (caching, retry window, fallback to lighter filter path).

I've attached trace samples and a CSV of failed filter-tool events.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Retail

Attachments: acme_latency_traces_20270420.zip; filter-call-failures-annotated.csv

From: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmeretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, k ar thik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed latency spikes tied to content-filter tool calls (pilot)

Sanjay —

Thanks for the traces, that helps. Short answer: yes, we can open a narrowly-scoped SLA exception for filter-dependent tool invocations while we implement two short-term mitigations. Proposed approach:

- Temporary SLA carve-out: exclude tool-invocation tail latency from the 300ms SLO for up to 30 days for the pilot routes you specify.
- Compensations we will apply immediately:
  - enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (reduces repeated tool invocations),
  - route non-critical requests to the lighter filter profile (same quality tier as agreed), and
  - apply a 500ms staged-retry with backoff on tool-call failures.

I'll loop in Marissa and Karthik to get approval on commercial/contract language and the security/compliance notes. If you want, Redwood can also propose a credit schedule if we miss agreed fallback targets.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Amendment_Draft_v1.pdf (draft; internal)

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed latency spikes tied to content-filter tool calls (pilot)

Marissa / team —

I reviewed the artifacts (thanks Sanjay). Technical summary and proposal:

- Root cause: intermittent high P95/P99 due to synchronous external moderation calls when the heavy filter profile is selected. These tool calls add non-deterministic network latency that we don't currently count separately in the SLO calculation.
- Short-term controls:
  1) Scoped SLA exclusion for external tool-invocation latency for the pilot routes (30 days).
  2) Logging and attestation: Redwood will provide per-request evidence showing when a request hit the heavy filter path and the fallback decision tree applied. We'll deliver a daily digest for the duration of the carve-out.
  3) Risk mitigations to be implemented within 7 days: KV caching warmup, non-blocking async moderation for low-risk requests, and a documented retry/backoff.

Acceptance criteria for removing the carve-out: 14-day rolling P99 for route <= 450ms with no more than two tool-call-induced incidents in 14 days. If we cannot meet that, we will provide escalating credits as defined in the attached SLA draft.

I'll prepare the technical appendix for the amendment.

— Karthik
Principal, Applied Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: technical-appendix (will be added to drive).

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmeretail.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, k ar thik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 17:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed latency spikes tied to content-filter tool calls (pilot)

Thanks — this plan looks reasonable. A couple of asks from legal/compliance before we sign:

- We need the carve-out to be scoped to the pilot API route and documented with explicit start/end times.
- Please include a clause that outlines what counts as a compensating mitigation (we'll accept async moderation for non-PII flows only).
- Acme Legal will redline the SLA amendment; please send a PDF and a Word trackable version.

Once we have that we can approve the temporary exception and proceed with the mitigations.

Sanjay
